title: How To Ensure Your Consistency For Next School Year
author: Michael Linsin
summary: Linsin offers a summer exercise to eliminate the hesitation that undermines consistent rule enforcement. Teachers are asked to list every misbehavior they've witnessed over the past several years, pair each one with the specific classroom rule it breaks, and then vividly visualize themselves calmly enforcing the consequence each time. The point is to pre-load the brain with a matched image of behavior and response, so that when the real misbehavior occurs, recognition and enforcement become reflexive rather than something the teacher has to reason through in the moment. He frames uncertainty about whether a rule was actually broken as the single biggest cause of inconsistency, since hesitation leads teachers to let infractions slide. The mental rehearsal step, he argues, cements the pairing so firmly that enforcement becomes automatic, comparing the effect to a referee who calls plays instantly and without doubt.
points: List every misbehavior observed over the past several years in as much detail as possible.
Pair each misbehavior with the specific class rule it violates, since knowing a rule was broken matters more than which one.
Visualize, in detail, calmly enforcing the correct consequence for each listed misbehavior to imprint the pairing on the brain.
Uncertainty about whether a rule was broken — not lack of will — is identified as the main cause of inconsistent enforcement.
The completed mental rehearsal creates a reflexive, near-automatic response that removes hesitation from real-time enforcement.
quotes: If you don’t know exactly what does and doesn’t constitute breaking your class rules —with zero gray area—then you can’t be consistent.
The uncertainty of whether or not a rule has been broken causes them to hesitate, second-guess, and ultimately move on without giving a consequence. This is extremely common.
This part of the exercise alone is worth its weight in gold because it begins imprinting your brain with an image of the misbehavior along with the accompanying rule.

It will light up the hippocampus and hippocampal gyrus regions of the brain. It’s like someone yelling “Now!” into your ear, enabling you to enforce without thought or stress or fear you’re getting it wrong.
You’ll be Pierluigi Collina, who is considered the greatest soccer referee of all time, calling ’em like you see ’em.
The exercise will eliminate every shred of incertitude and allow you to be truly consistent, day in and day out.
